2610.07083.title: Graph-Based Recognition of Simulated Train-Driver States From Facial and Upper-Body Keypoints
2610.07083.paper_summary: Driver fatigue poses a significant challenge to railway safety, with traditional systems like the dead-man switch offering limited and basic alertness checks. This study presents a vision-based monitoring system that relies solely on a single front-facing RGB camera and a graph neural network to classify simulated train-driver states into alert, not-alert, and an emergency class comprising acted emergency-like behaviours. To optimize input representations for the model, an ablation study was performed, comparing three feature configurations: skeletal-only, facial-only, and a combination of both. Experimental results show that combining facial and skeletal features yields the highest accuracy (81%) for the three-class model under the light condition, outperforming models that use only facial or skeletal features. Furthermore, the combination of facial and skeletal features achieves 99% accuracy in the alert/not alert classification in light condition. Additionally, we introduced a controlled RGB video dataset containing alert, not alert, and acted emergency-like behaviours recorded under three illumination conditions. These contributions represent a step toward passive and non-contact train-driver state recognition based on facial and upper-body dynamics.
2610.07083.paper_summary_zh: 駕駛疲勞對鐵路安全構成了重大挑戰，傳統系統如死男人開關提供的警覺性檢查有限且基本。這項研究提出了一種基於視覺的監測系統，僅依賴一個前置RGB攝影機和圖神經網絡將模擬的火車駕駛員狀態分類為警覺、不警覺，以及包含模擬緊急行為的緊急類別。為了優化模型的輸入表示，進行了一項消融研究，比較了三種特徵配置：僅骨架、僅面部，以及兩者的組合。實驗結果顯示，結合面部和骨架特徵在光照條件下的三類模型中達到了最高準確率（81%），超過了僅使用面部或骨架特徵的模型。此外，在光照條件下，面部和骨架特徵的結合在警覺/不警覺分類中達到了99%的準確率。此外，我們引入了一個受控的RGB視頻數據集，包含在三種照明條件下錄製的警覺、不警覺和模擬緊急行為。這些貢獻代表了基於面部和上半身動態的被動和非接觸式火車駕駛員狀態識別的一步。
